issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (UML and task text), but both the template and the solution use the method name singFarmSong(). This name mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement or where to add the song-printing logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere (including the UML and task text), or rename the template and solution method to printFarmSong(). Ensure the example Main and UML use the same identifier so students know which method to implement.

issues.description: The UML and task description specify a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal), but the template's private method has the Animal parameter commented out (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), while the solution correctly declares singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The commented-out parameter in the template creates a signature mismatch against the specification and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the template method signature to match the UML/specification: change the template's private method to singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This ensures students can call the helper with an Animal argument as described in the task and mirrors the solution's signature.
